hero.title: Oil Nears $110 as Middle East Conflict Sends Global Markets Into Turmoil
hero.description: Brent crude has climbed to almost $110 a barrel as attacks and shipping disruptions linked to the US–Iran conflict raise fears of a prolonged global energy shock.

breaking: 🛢️ Brent crude reaches almost $110 a barrel as Middle East shipping disruptions intensify.
🇺🇸🇮🇷 US–Iran tensions continue to threaten energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.
🇾🇪 Iran-aligned Houthi forces have seized Yemen's strategic port city of Mocha, increasing risks to Red Sea shipping.
🇺🇸 US producer prices rose 0.4% in August, strengthening expectations of possible Federal Reserve tightening.
🇳🇬 Dangote Refinery secures at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October delivery.
🇳🇬 A Federal High Court in Lagos keeps an interim order in force in the Dangote–NMDPRA dispute.
🇪🇺 ECB raises its policy rate to 2.50% as energy-driven inflation risks intensify.
🇺🇸 US 10-year Treasury yield approaches 5% as global bond markets come under pressure.
🇺🇦 NATO allies reportedly disrupted a suspected Russian exercise involving technology designed to target critical undersea cables near Svalbard.
🇺🇸🇺🇸 Friday marks 25 years since the September 11, 2001 attacks that killed almost 3,000 people.

featured.title: Oil Shock Deepens as Global Shipping Routes Come Under Pressure
featured.content: Brent crude climbed to about $109.97 a barrel on Friday, putting the benchmark on course for a weekly gain of almost 13%. US West Texas Intermediate also moved above $103. The latest surge reflects continuing attacks and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, together with the seizure of Yemen's Mocha port by Iran-aligned Houthi forces. The combination is raising fears that a prolonged conflict could keep energy prices elevated and feed inflation around the world.

articles.title: US–Iran Conflict Keeps Energy Markets on Edge
articles.content: Oil markets remain highly sensitive to developments around the Gulf and Red Sea. Brent has risen almost 13% this week, while both major crude benchmarks are heading towards their first weekly close above $100 since May. Analysts warn that a further escalation could push prices substantially higher.

articles.title: Houthi Capture of Mocha Raises Red Sea Shipping Concerns
articles.content: Iran-aligned Houthi forces have taken control of Yemen's port city of Mocha, adding another strategic risk to commercial traffic near the Bab el-Mandeb. The development comes as shipping through the wider region is already being disrupted by the conflict.

articles.title: US Producer Prices Add to Federal Reserve Rate Debate
articles.content: US producer prices increased 0.4% in August, while annual producer-price inflation reached 5.4%. Rising energy and service costs have strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve may need to maintain or tighten policy despite concerns about economic growth.

articles.title: US Treasury Yield Moves Close to 5%
articles.content: The benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.9708%, its highest level in three years. Investors are reassessing inflation and interest-rate risks as oil prices surge and government borrowing costs rise.

articles.title: 25 Years Since September 11 Attacks
articles.content: The United States marks the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks. Nearly 3,000 people were killed when hijacked aircraft struck the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and a field in Pennsylvania. The attacks reshaped US national security policy and had consequences that continue to influence international affairs today.

articles.title: Dangote Secures 16 Million Barrels of Nigerian Crude
articles.content: Dangote Refinery has secured at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October, equivalent to roughly 520,000 barrels per day. The volume represents a substantial share of the refinery's 700,000-barrel-per-day capacity and comes as global crude supplies face disruption.

articles.title: Dangote–NMDPRA Court Dispute Continues
articles.content: A Federal High Court in Lagos has allowed an interim order protecting Dangote Refinery's position in its dispute with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority to remain in force. The court deferred substantive arguments on jurisdiction until the relevant applications are ready for determination.

articles.title: Kano Police Arrest Two Over Dan Shagamu Killing
articles.content: Kano State Police say two suspects have been arrested in connection with the killing of political commentator Ibrahim Khalil, popularly known as Dan Shagamu. Police said he was attacked at his residence in Gaida, Kumbotso, and that investigations and forensic procedures are continuing to establish the circumstances and motive.

articles.title: ECB Raises Interest Rate to 2.50%
articles.content: The European Central Bank has raised its policy rate by 0.25 percentage points to 2.50%, its second increase this year. The decision reflects renewed inflation concerns as sharply higher energy prices threaten to keep consumer prices elevated across the euro area.

articles.title: European Bond Markets Face Fresh Pressure
articles.content: European bond yields have climbed sharply as investors react to higher oil prices and expectations of further monetary tightening. The ECB's latest rate increase has added to concerns about borrowing costs for governments, businesses and households.

articles.title: NATO Allies Reportedly Disrupted Russian Undersea Cable Exercise
articles.content: A report says NATO allies Britain, Norway and the United States tracked and confronted Russian vessels near the Svalbard archipelago after identifying an alleged exercise involving technology that could be used against critical undersea cables. Officials said no cables were damaged and Russia has denied sabotage operations in NATO countries.

articles.title: Japan's Wholesale Inflation Adds Pressure on Central Bank
articles.content: Japan's wholesale inflation rose 7.6% year-on-year in August, strengthening the case for the Bank of Japan to consider another interest-rate increase. The yen has also come under pressure as global energy prices rise.

articles.title: Global Markets React to Oil Shock
articles.content: Global bond and equity markets have come under pressure as investors reassess inflation and interest-rate risks. The US dollar remains relatively strong, while the 10-year Treasury yield is close to 5%. Oil's nearly 13% weekly gain has become the dominant factor driving market sentiment.

articles.title: Oil Could Stay Above $100 If Conflict Persists
articles.content: Energy analysts warn that crude prices could rise further if attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure continue. Brent briefly approached $110 on Friday, while some analysts have warned of substantially higher prices if supply disruptions deepen.

articles.title: Undersea Cables Become a Growing Security Concern
articles.content: The reported Russian exercise near Svalbard has renewed attention on the vulnerability of subsea communication infrastructure. Undersea fibre-optic cables carry huge volumes of international data, making them increasingly important to national security and economic resilience.

morningSummary: Good morning. Oil and global markets dominate today's headlines as the US–Iran conflict continues to disrupt energy and shipping routes. Brent crude has climbed to almost $110 a barrel and is up nearly 13% this week. In Nigeria, Dangote Refinery has secured at least 16 million barrels of crude for October, while its legal dispute with NMDPRA continues in court. The ECB has raised its policy rate to 2.50%, while US inflation data has increased expectations of possible Federal Reserve tightening. Today also marks 25 years since the September 11 attacks, a moment of remembrance for those who lost their lives and reflection on the global consequences that followed.
bigQuestion: If oil prices remain above $100 for several months, what should governments prioritise most — protecting consumers from rising costs, increasing domestic energy production, or reducing dependence on fossil fuels?
